title: Practical Lab (Python)
description: The CCMAS Python practical course: modular programming with modules and namespaces, reading and writing files, classes and objects, inheritance and polymorphism, installing and using external libraries, data analysis with Pandas, and working with APIs and web data. Built from the COS 203 practical lab note, the Advanced OOP, External Libraries and API lesson materials, and the Python Basics textbook in the course folder.

topics.title: Modular Programming, Modules and Namespaces
topics.summary: Modular programming breaks a program into smaller, manageable, reusable components called modules. A Python module is a file of code that can be imported into other files; each module has its own namespace, and the import statement has variations such as import ... as and from ... import.

topics.title: Reading and Writing Files
topics.summary: Python reads and writes text files by opening a file object in a mode such as read, write or append, ideally inside a with statement so the file is closed automatically. Methods such as read, readlines, write and writelines move text in and out of files.
subtopics: Opening files with open() and Path.open()
File modes r, w and a

topics.title: Classes and Objects in Python
topics.summary: Classes create user-defined data structures. A class is a blueprint that defines attributes and methods; an instance is an object built from the class that contains real data. The __init__ method sets each instance's attributes through self.
subtopics: Why classes: limits of lists for records

topics.title: Inheritance, Polymorphism and Special Methods
topics.summary: Inheritance lets a child class reuse a parent's attributes and methods, with super() to call the parent. Polymorphism lets different classes respond in their own way to the same method call, method overriding replaces a parent's method in the child, and the special methods __str__ and __repr__ give objects readable output.

topics.title: External Libraries and pip
topics.summary: Python's Standard Library cannot do everything, so programmers install third-party libraries from PyPI with pip. A requirements.txt file records a project's packages, and a virtual environment isolates each project's packages. Popular libraries include NumPy, Pandas, Matplotlib, Requests and scikit-learn.
subtopics: The Standard Library and third-party libraries

topics.title: Data Analysis with Pandas
topics.summary: Pandas is the standard Python library for tabular data. Its core structures are the Series and the DataFrame. Students load data from files, inspect it, select rows with loc and iloc, filter with boolean indexing, add columns, handle missing data, sort, group and merge.
subtopics: Filtering, adding columns and missing data

topics.title: Working with APIs and Web Data
topics.summary: An API is an agreed way for one program to ask another for data or an action, usually returning JSON over HTTP. Students read and write JSON with the json module, send GET and POST requests with the requests library, handle status codes, errors, timeouts and rate limits, and extract data from HTML responsibly with BeautifulSoup.
subtopics: What an API is and the request-response cycle
GET and POST with requests; errors and timeouts
